author_rationale: Denominator excludes unknown receipt status; failed outer transactions remain included.
Uses actual receipt gas, not the gas limit; no ETH/token conflation.
Uses block metadata rather than counting sampled outer transactions.
Beneficiary is the fee recipient, not an asserted validator identity.
Explicit UTC hour extraction; all stored outer rows are counted.
Receipt contract address identifies creation, not the transaction recipient.
HAVING requires both outcomes for the same ordered endpoint pair.
Declared outer value is not a net balance change; self-address equality is deliberate.
Boundary values 25% and 75% enter the next bucket; missing gas is excluded.
A transfer row is a log event; no join multiplies event rows.
Multiplicity is measured per transaction and token, not per endpoint.
Missing decimals/cast metadata can make normalization NULL; no amount is fabricated.
Metadata-only query; symbol is not assumed to uniquely identify a token.
Latest-per-address dimension metadata; an empty list is a valid coverage observation.
A sample-coverage diagnostic, expected to be empty on complete transaction coverage.
Join uses hash plus block identity; transaction value is grouped, never summed across logs.
NOT EXISTS avoids fanout and keeps transactions without transfer events.
Question specifies observed-date rows, including partial windows at the start.
Metadata snapshot is not a time series; UTC window supplies the benchmark cutoff context.
UNION ALL followed by distinct address count avoids double counting roles.
All known recipient addresses participate; unknown status is included only in total.
Receipt gas summarizes outer calls to the full owner address set.
All outcomes retained; declared value is not claimed to be realized ETH flow.
Distinct sender count is computed after owner union, not summed across wallets.
Includes creation transactions in count; their NULL recipient is excluded by DISTINCT.
Owner address union is essential even for zero-value outer calls.
Counterparty ranking aggregates all owner sender addresses before limiting.
UTC hour grouping follows union of all dictionary-known recipients.
Positive declared value predicate belongs to both union and single-address checks.
OR selects each outer row once; directional counts intentionally overlap.
Event counts, not normalized amounts across heterogeneous tokens.
Known owner sender addresses are unioned before pair ranking.
OR prevents duplicate rows when both event endpoints belong to the owner.
A transaction may emit multiple inbound events across owner addresses.
Returning contributions of all active known addresses exposes representative-wallet loss.
Raw numeric cast checks do not imply normalized ERC20 amounts.
Different projection and aggregation intent from receipt outcome analysis.
Known address membership is complete even when some addresses are inactive.
Canonical owner HTX avoids the ambiguous token alias Huobi.
Separate token identities; internal events do not double the either-role total.
Historical name uniquely resolves to OKX, and fraction uses only known statuses.
Protocol owner Curve DEX, not the Curve governance token.
TC is a dictionary alias of the privacy-service owner; all known endpoints included.
Version-qualified alias avoids ambiguous Uniswap family resolution.
Aggregates outer receipt gas for every known V3 endpoint, independent of token events.
V4 is a distinct owner, not a renamed V3 address set.
Alias denotes the known L1 bridge owner, not all transactions on an L2 chain.
Gateway alias uses endpoint role; token identity is unrestricted.
Noncanonical owner alias, with sender aggregation after recipient-address union.
Punctuation alias is dictionary-bound; NULL receipt status is not silently dropped.
Declared-value diagnostic, explicitly not balance change or realized ETH settlement.
Short alias resolves to OSL HK; null recipient rows are explicitly counted.
Token ticker alias is token identity; local normalized totals use DOUBLE, not exact accounting.
Raw cast range differs locally from BigQuery BIGNUMERIC; full parity remains pending.
LINK uniquely resolves to Chainlink; invalid cast values enter neither raw bucket.
Alias refers to protocol endpoints, not a token ticker.
Dictionary service alias names one owner; it is not a request for all mixers.
Spaced alias is unambiguous in the pinned dictionary; bare PancakeSwap is ambiguous.
CCIP is a bridge owner distinct from the Chainlink token contract.
First/last timestamps apply to event receipts, not outer transaction senders.
All thirty dictionary ExchangeAccount owners, not all exchanges on Ethereum.
Protocol class is operational DEX endpoints, not governance-token holders.
Includes only dictionary lending endpoints; token owners with similar names are excluded.
Only labeled bridge endpoints; sending a bridge token is insufficient.
OR selects union of endpoint roles without doubling internal rows.
Class membership remains annotated even if this small class has no sampled activity.
Both endpoint predicates are required. Class direction either describes roles, not SQL OR.
Distinct counts are recomputed across the owner's complete labeled endpoint set.
Money market maps to the dictionary LendingProtocol class, with explicit pooling.
Declared call values do not assert completed bridge transfers or L2 outcomes.
Same-owner condition differs from exchange-to-exchange activity in general.
Zero invalid values are retained; absence of errors is not absence of events.
Class-level request is distinct from the singular service alias 'the mixer'.
Two distinct class mentions and directional targets; no token-owner join substitution.
Two endpoint class predicates; outer calls, not inferred cross-chain settlement.
Strict gas threshold applies to actual receipt gas, not the declared gas limit.
Outer-row anti-join; activity is not counted in token-event rows.
Known staking class only; distinct hour-of-day values range from zero through 23.
Contract-only owner sets may not originate outer transactions; an empty result is plausible.
Dictionary inventory, no transaction/event fact and no activity direction.
Received selects outer to_address; declared positive value does not imply receipt success.
Sent selects outer from_address; unknown receipt statuses contribute to total.
Either is a set union, not outgoing alone and not a sum of role counts.
Ordered endpoint pair has two distinct entity direction annotations.
Transfer-event sender is not the outer transaction sender.
Received constrains the event endpoint, not the token contract nor outer recipient.
Either-role filter and both-role output are different Boolean conditions.
Entity direction applies to outer calls; log endpoints may be unrelated.
First groups logs by outer hash, then counts qualifying transactions once.
One row per token log; the positive raw-value bucket does not normalize units.
A token contract used as outer recipient has endpoint role for this intent.
Absence of logs requires a second fact and NOT EXISTS.
Each entity constrains a different fact: outer sender versus log recipient.
Negative control: reverted outer transactions normally retain no logs; preserve a justified empty answer.
Token mention maps to token_address, not sender or recipient.
The ticker names an endpoint here; token_address need not equal the mentioned contract.
Explicit literal has explicit_address scope and known owner WETH.
Self-event comparison does not make the named token an endpoint target.
Two entity targets have different roles and independent identity sets.
A token contract may be queried as an endpoint even when there are no matching sample events.
